wren.title: The Poacher
lines: Wren knew every deer track in the vale before the vale knew him.
He poached to feed a starving village. Now the village is trying to eat him.
"Funny thing about mercy," he says, nocking an arrow. "It keeps you in practice."
He watches the churchyard at dusk. The first ones out of the ground never come from the graves he'd expect.

maud.title: The Gravedigger
lines: Maud dug every grave in Hollowmere for thirty years. Knows each one by name and depth.
"No respect for craftsmanship," she mutters, shovel on her shoulder. "They keep checking out early."
But she's noticed something the others haven't: her graves opened LAST.
Whatever wakes the dead — it started somewhere else. Somewhere higher. Up where the bell tolls.

corvus.title: The Plague Doctor
lines: Corvus came to cure a plague. He stayed because there wasn't one.
His notes are meticulous: the fevers, the deaths, the risings. All in the wrong order.
"A sickness has a source," he says through the beak. "This has an INVITATION."
He keeps mixing his vials. Whatever answered the invitation dislikes them immensely.

roland.title: The Disgraced Knight
lines: They say Ser Roland fled Castle Vane the night it fell. They spit when they say it.
He lets them spit. Armor takes worse than spit.
But ask him what he saw in the chapel that night — what the king was DOING — and the wall of steel goes quiet.
"I didn't run from the dead," he says at last, hand on the great blade. "I ran to warn the living. No one listened."

ansel.title: The Heretic Monk
lines: They burned Ansel's writings and unmade his vows. His crime: asking what the church sealed inside the castle chapel.
"Excommunication," he says, swinging his censer, "has done wonders for my schedule."
He was right, of course. The priests knew. They sealed the chapel the night the bell first tolled — and never said why.
Every night he fights is a prayer. Every dawn, an argument won.

hollow_king.title: The Hollow King
lines: The king of Castle Vane lost his queen and his daughter to fever in a single week.
So he went down to the sealed chapel, and he rang the bell that must never be rung, and he bargained.
Something answered. It was generous. It returns the dead — everyone's dead — every night, forever.
He is still half-alive inside the bargain, hollowed out to hold it. The cursed blade drinks what it kills because HE must.
"I bought this night," he says, and draws. "The least I can do is stand it."

sin_eater.title: The Sin-Eater
lines: They called for her at every deathbed in Hollowmere, and paid her in bread and silence.
She ate the sins of the dying over their cooling hands, so their souls would go clean. She carried all of it, and said nothing.
"Everyone else runs from the dead," she says, lifting the bowl. "I have been swallowing them my whole life. What is one more night?"
When the graves opened, the vale remembered whose fault it wasn't, and whose burden it always had been.
